title: Enhanced rock weathering measurement and verification
bottleneck: Spreading crushed silicate rock on fields to absorb CO2 is cheap in theory, but proving how much carbon was actually removed is extremely difficult: weathering rates depend on soil chemistry, rainfall, and grain size, and the signal is a tiny change in soil carbon against a noisy background. Without cheap, credible measurement, rock weathering cannot generate trustworthy carbon credits or count toward national targets.
why_it_blocks: Measurement is the whole ballgame for CDR: unverifiable removal is worthless to buyers and policymakers. The MRV gap keeps enhanced weathering as a promising idea that cannot yet transact in carbon markets at scale.
current_state: Field trials across the US, UK, and Malaysia are building the empirical base, and startups are selling early credits with model-based estimates. But standardized, low-cost MRV protocols accepted by registries and regulators do not yet exist.
